newsitem.title: CHINA: China's B share indices end down, A indices up.
newsitem.headline: China's B share indices end down, A indices up.

text.p: China's B shares ended down on Tuesday on a technical correction, sparked by concerns over poor 1996 annual results which are expected to flood the market ahead of the April 30 deadline, brokers said.
But A shares closed up on bullish sentiment, they said.
The Shanghai B index fell 0.973 points or 1.11 percent to 86.557 points on volume of 44.874 million shares worth $26.931 million, compared with $36.359 million yuan on Monday.
Brokers said selling in shares expected to post poor 1996 results pulled the index down, but market sentiment was still good following the solid gains of the past few sessions.
Huaxin Cement 1996 net profits plunged 63.87 percent, the company said on Tuesday. Its poor result led to selling in other stocks expected to issue poor results for 1996, brokers said.
Huaxin was the second biggest loser on unwinding selling, slipping $0.022 or 7.43 percent to $0.274 on volume of 1.9 million shares.
"Active bargain-hunting prevented the index from losing further," one broker said. "Most investors believe that the market can see the index hitting 100 points in the near future."
Brokers said they expected support around 85 points.
Shanghai Automation Instrument was the biggest loser on expectations of unpromising results, tumbling $0.020 or 7.93 percent to $0.232 on volume of 1.1 million shares.
Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor was the most actively traded stock on talk of possible lower-than-expected results, slipping $0.020 or 2.91 percent to $0.666 on volume of 3.8 million shares.
The Shenzhen B share index dipped 3.40 points or 1.87 percent to end at 178.39 on turnover of HK$199.4 million against Monday's HK$368.4 million.
"Caution is likely to characterise the market later this week as the remaining B share firms are expected to publish weak 1996 results," an analyst with a major Chinese brokerage said.
Television maker Shenzhen Konka was the biggest B share loser, sliding HK$0.63 or 5.34 percent to HK$11.17 on volume of 1.07 million shares due to profit-taking.
Wafangdian was the most actively traded share, slipping HK$0.11 to HK$6.94. on volume of 3.57 million shares. The stock had risen nearly 40 percent over the past few sessions.

The Shanghai A index rose 4.096 points or 0.29 percent to 1,428.202 on volume of 964.9 million shares worth 11.7 billion yuan. The SSE30 index edged up 1.037 points or 0.03 percent to 3,683.373 points.
The Shenzhen A share index rose 1.69 points or 0.36 percent to finish at 473.19 on turnover of 10.6 billion yuan.
